numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For large |linpred| (e.g. |linpred| up to 1e4), the Logit log-likelihood computed as log(cdf(q*linpred)) overflows in exp, the cdf underflows to 0, and log(0) returns -inf with RuntimeWarnings (overflow encountered in exp); returned loglikeobs entries are -inf.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Log-likelihood values should be finite and correct for extreme linpreds without RuntimeWarnings, equal to -log(1+exp(-z)) (about -z for large negative z), cross-checked against scipy.special.log_expit at rtol=1e-14 in the regression test.
trigger_conditions: Large magnitude linear predictor, e.g. |linpred| up to 1e4, causing exp overflow in the Logit cdf for large negative q*linpred
Overflow warnings raised as RuntimeWarnings (overflow encountered in exp) under simplefilter('error') in the regression test
Integer or boolean endog, which made q*linpred integer-typed and required casting to float64 for logaddexp on some numpy builds
Complex inputs from complex-step differentiation (test_numdiff TestGradLogit) which need a piecewise log1p form

input_output_examples.input: Logit loglikeobs with |linpred| up to 1e4 (regression test test_logit_loglikeobs_extreme_linpred in tests/test_discrete.py)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: -inf entries and overflow encountered in exp RuntimeWarning
input_output_examples.expected_output: finite values, zero RuntimeWarnings, matching scipy.special.log_expit at rtol=1e-14

oracle_clues: Regression test asserts finiteness with simplefilter('error') so no RuntimeWarnings are allowed
TestGradLogit uses decimal=11 / rtol=1e-9 tolerances for score and hess
Complex-step score matches analytic score to 1e-12

numerical_characteristics.dtype: float64 (integer/boolean endog promoted to float64; the passages do not state a dtype for the complex path)
numerical_characteristics.precision: Complex-step derivatives are kept at machine precision; the regression test asserts rtol=1e-14
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: |linpred| up to 1e4 (regression test uses z from -1e4 to 1e4 with n=50)
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: Regression test: rtol=1e-14 for loglikeobs and loglike; TestGradLogit: decimal=11 / rtol=1e-9; complex-step score vs analytic score: 1e-12
category_specific_evidence: The violated property is the identity log Λ(z) = -log(1 + exp(-z)); the original log(cdf(z)) form overflowed in exp for large |z|, producing -inf loglikeobs values and RuntimeWarnings (gh-3923).
The fixed code computes z = -q*linpred and returns np.sum(-_log_1pexp(z)), with _log_1pexp using logaddexp for real inputs and a piecewise log1p(exp(w)) form for complex inputs.

The regression test test_logit_loglikeobs_extreme_linpred uses n=50, z=np.linspace(-1e4, 1e4, 50), an integer endog of ones, and params [0.0, 1.0]; it asserts finiteness under warnings-as-errors and agreement with scipy.special.log_expit(z) at rtol=1e-14.
